concerns.concern: Bulk superconductivity is not shown. The resistance drops only about 10–25% below onset, never reaches zero, and no diamagnetic or shielding-fraction measurement is given, so filamentary or minority-phase superconductivity cannot be excluded.
concerns.quote: Zero resistance is never reached, and the "onset" is a broad maximum or kink on a semiconducting background.

concerns.concern: The authors attribute the low-temperature anomaly in x = 2.4 to other intergrowth Ruddlesden–Popper phases without evidence. This leaves open which phase actually hosts the 92–98 K signal.
concerns.quote: That attribution is made without evidence and leaves open which phase hosts the 92–98 K signal.

concerns.concern: The radio-frequency (RF) anomalies near 98 K vary in shape and sign across frequency, sample, channel and sweep direction, and are tiny relative to background. No physical model explains why superconductivity would produce such varied responses.
concerns.quote: No physical model explains why a superconducting transition should produce such varied responses in this geometry.

concerns.concern: The headline claim of pushing the Tc frontier to near 100 K rests on the RF data alone. Without controls it should be described only as a possible signature in the title and abstract.
concerns.quote: 98 K should be described as a "possible signature" in the title and abstract, not a new Tc frontier.

concerns.concern: Extrinsic origins of the RF anomaly are not excluded: density-wave remnants, Nd magnetism, cell/gasket/medium anomalies, structural anomalies or thermometry artefacts. Field-dependence, pressure-dependence and empty-cell background controls are needed.
concerns.quote: Without discriminating controls, extrinsic origins remain plausible

concerns.concern: The BSCCO validation of the RF method is inadequate. It was done at 0 GPa on a film rather than in a loaded high-pressure cell, and the film's cited 94 K Tc was not independently checked.
concerns.quote: that validation was done at 0 GPa on a film, not in a loaded high-pressure cell

concerns.concern: The Methods call the second harmonic the key signature, but the figures show the real and imaginary parts of the transmitted signal. It is unclear which quantity is plotted.
concerns.quote: It is unclear whether the plotted quantity is the second harmonic or the fundamental.

concerns.concern: The RF Tc exceeds the resistive onset by about 5 K, the reverse of the usual ordering. The paper offers two mutually inconsistent qualitative explanations instead of a quantitative one.
concerns.quote: two mutually inconsistent qualitative explanations are offered

concerns.concern: The RF runs used an ammonia borane (NH₃BH₃) pressure medium, unlike transport and XRD. Possible chemical reaction or hydrogen uptake by the oxygen-labile nickelate is not addressed.
concerns.quote: Possible chemical reaction of ammonia borane or its decomposition products (hydrogen/nitrogen) with an oxygen-labile nickelate, including hydrogen uptake, is not addressed.

concerns.concern: Sensor–sample thermal lag in the RF cell could account for several kelvin, as the cooling/warming asymmetry suggests. Thermometer placement and sweep rates are not described.
concerns.quote: Sensor–sample thermal lag in the RF DAC could account for several kelvin, and the cooling/warming asymmetry suggests exactly this.

concerns.concern: RF and transport measurements were made at different, uncertain pressures and possibly on different sample batches. This makes their Tc values hard to compare.
concerns.quote: The RF pressures (36 ± 4 GPa; 41 GPa) are uncertain and differ from the transport pressure (34.9 GPa).

concerns.concern: The 'highest Tc among nickelates' claim rests on about 1 K over Sm-doped samples. The onset criterion is undefined, so this margin is within uncertainty.
concerns.quote: Arrow placement at a broad maximum or kink, with no stated method (deviation point, derivative, intersecting tangents).

concerns.concern: The pressure calibration switches from ruby to diamond Raman at 30 GPa with a 5–10% discrepancy. This gives ±2–3 GPa uncertainty in the critical pressure window.
concerns.quote: The calibration switches from ruby fluorescence to diamond Raman at exactly 30 GPa, with a stated 5–10% discrepancy.

concerns.concern: Data seem to come from a single run per composition, with no Tc error bars or statistics across cells or samples.
concerns.quote: Data appear to come from one run per composition (Run 1: x = 2.1; Run 2: x = 2.4), with no Tc error bars or statistics

concerns.concern: Competing reports of Tc above 90 K are not all cited and compared.
concerns.quote: cite and compare all competing >90 K reports

concerns.concern: The 'universal' linear Tc versus c-axis relation relies on selected points and ignores that Tc saturates or falls under further compression while c keeps shrinking. An inconvenient film point is also excluded post hoc.
concerns.quote: A monotonic Tc(c) therefore cannot be universal. The inconvenient La₃Ni₂O₇/NdGaO₃ film point is excluded post hoc.

concerns.concern: Lattice parameter c and Tc in the correlation come from mismatched conditions: room-temperature XRD in Ne versus low-temperature transport in KBr. Some compositions and literature points have no high-pressure XRD of their own.
concerns.quote: Thermal contraction and medium-dependent stress can shift c by amounts comparable to the spread in Fig. 5b.

concerns.concern: The Tc–c compilation mixes unlike samples, such as films with different substrates, strain and substitution. It also includes unverifiable data from an unpublished paper in preparation.
concerns.quote: Some key Sm data come from an unpublished "paper in preparation" (Ref. 42) that cannot be verified.

concerns.concern: No fit statistics or slope uncertainty are given. The slope is set by two disjoint clusters (bulk and films) that differ in many other ways, and the correlation within the bulk cluster is weak.
concerns.quote: No slope uncertainty, R², correlation coefficient, residual analysis or treatment of errors in c or Tc is given.

concerns.concern: Claiming interlayer exchange J⊥ is 'demonstrated' as the dominant pairing mechanism does not follow. The c axis is a poor proxy for J⊥, no Ni–O–Ni geometry or independent J⊥ estimate is given, and many alternative descriptors are untested.
concerns.quote: A correlation with c therefore cannot single out J⊥ over alternatives

concerns.concern: Only nominal compositions are reported. Saturating lattice parameters suggest the real Nd content of x = 2.4 may be lower than nominal or inhomogeneous, undermining the record-substitution claim and the distinction between x = 2.1 and 2.4.
concerns.quote: The real Nd content of "x = 2.4," which carries the ~98 K RF claim, may therefore be lower than nominal or inhomogeneous.

concerns.concern: Phase purity is asserted rather than shown. Rietveld fits lack reliability factors and occupancies, lab XRD cannot exclude polytypes or intergrowths, and invoking intergrowths for x = 2.4 contradicts the pure-phase claim.
concerns.quote: Lab powder XRD cannot reliably exclude 1313/2222/4310 polytypes, La₄Ni₃O₁₀/La₂NiO₄ intergrowths or stacking faults.

concerns.concern: Oxygen content is not measured, although it strongly affects both the density wave and superconductivity.
concerns.quote: Oxygen content δ, which strongly affects both the density wave and superconductivity in La₃Ni₂O₇₋δ, is not measured.

concerns.concern: Ambient-pressure resistivity is non-monotonic in x, contradicting the claim that samples become monotonically more insulating. It may reflect oxygen or disorder changes rather than intrinsic doping.
concerns.quote: contrary to the statement that samples become monotonically "more insulating."

concerns.concern: The coincidence of the structural transition and the onset of superconductivity is inferred across about 200 K and different pressure media. The data are not precise enough to support it.
concerns.quote: The coincidence of the structural (Amam→I4/mmm) and superconducting boundaries is inferred, not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: High-pressure XRD is missing for x = 1.5 and 2.4, yet both appear in the phase diagram as if the structure–superconductivity correspondence applied to them.
concerns.quote: High-pressure XRD is absent for x = 1.5 and 2.4, yet both appear in the phase diagram (Fig. 4)

concerns.concern: The large susceptibility rise is presumably dominated by the Nd³⁺ Curie contribution. Without subtracting it, it says nothing about Ni magnetism or exchange.
concerns.quote: presumably dominated by the Nd³⁺ 4f Curie contribution and says nothing about Ni exchange without subtraction

concerns.concern: The spin-density-wave transition temperature is inferred only from weak resistivity-derivative kinks that change shape at high x. There is no microscopic confirmation.
concerns.quote: There is no μSR, NMR, neutron or χ-anomaly confirmation.

concerns.concern: The rising spin-density-wave trend contradicts Ref. 34, which reports an unaltered density-wave transition in Nd-doped La₃Ni₂O₇. This conflict is not discussed.
concerns.quote: The trend also contradicts Ref. 34, which reports an "unaltered density wave transition" in Nd-doped La₃Ni₂O₇; this conflict is not discussed.

concerns.concern: A higher ambient-pressure spin-density-wave temperature does not imply a higher J⊥ in the pressurized tetragonal phase, where the spin-density wave is suppressed.
concerns.quote: an increased ambient-pressure T_SDW does not equate to an increased J⊥ in the pressurized tetragonal phase

concerns.concern: The upper-critical-field values come from a long single-band Ginzburg–Landau extrapolation of onset points over a narrow field range, with no error bars.
concerns.quote: The onset criterion inflates Hc2 and is sensitive to background curvature. No error bars are given.

concerns.concern: The stated trend that doping lowers the upper critical field contradicts the numbers, since x = 2.4 gives the larger value. No undoped reference measured the same way is provided.
concerns.quote: Yet the more heavily doped x = 2.4 sample gives the larger value at a lower Tc (85 K at 40.3 GPa).

concerns.concern: Tc values are quoted inconsistently across the abstract, text and figure captions for x = 2.1 and 2.4.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 2a caption assigns the orange 93 K arrow to x = 2.4, whereas the text assigns 93 K to x = 2.1.

concerns.concern: In the field series, the zero-field curve behaves qualitatively differently from the in-field curves. This raises doubts about sample or thermal-cycle stability.
concerns.quote: the 0 T curve is qualitatively different from the in-field curves (metallic down to low T versus upturns)

concerns.concern: The claim that superconductivity is seen at all doping levels is unsupported, because x = 0.3 and 0.6 are absent from the transport data.
concerns.quote: The claim that superconductivity is observed "across all doping levels" is not supported for x = 0.3 and 0.6

concerns.concern: RF frequency, pressure and real/imaginary channel labels are inconsistent between Fig. 3, Extended Data Fig. 5 and the captions.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 3e text/caption gives S1 warming at 25 MHz, while the panel and ED Fig. 5f give 20 MHz.

concerns.concern: Parts of the Extended Data Fig. 5 caption are misplaced in the reference list.
concerns.quote: Parts of the ED Fig. 5 caption are misplaced in the reference list.

concerns.concern: The composition list in the Fig. 5 legend does not match its caption.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 5 legend's composition list is not consistent with its caption.

concerns.concern: Figs. 4 and 5 use different composition subsets without explanation.
concerns.quote: Figs. 4 and 5 use different composition subsets

concerns.concern: The cited ionic radii appear to mix coordination numbers. They should be taken consistently from Shannon tables for the relevant coordination.
concerns.quote: appear to mix coordination numbers and should be taken consistently from Shannon tables

concerns.concern: The phrase 'Sm-doped analogue (x = 1.5)' is unclear and should be clarified.
concerns.quote: The phrasing "Sm-doped analogue (x = 1.5)" should be clarified.

concerns.concern: There are typographical errors to fix.
concerns.quote: "Rigabu" → "Rigaku" and "adoped" → "adopted."
